第69届柏林国际电影节(2019)
　　主竞赛单元 最佳短片(提名)

writer.name: 瓦伦·萨辛德兰 Varun Sasindran

director.name: 瓦伦·萨辛德兰 Varun Sasindran

introduction: 1992年波斯尼亚战争。在波斯尼亚和黑塞哥维那北部有奥马尔斯卡集中营，根据塞尔维亚的报告，集中营是一个集合点和调查中心。1992年5月至8月，数千人在那里被拘留、折磨、强奸和谋杀。现在是阿塞洛-米塔尔公司的工厂。到目前为止，在那里被谋杀的人还没有被纪念。这部电影是根据努斯瑞塔·西瓦克痛苦的回忆改编的，他在战争爆发前一直担任法官。她被送到奥马尔斯卡集中营，不得不在厨房工作。从那里她可以观察到暴行，自己成了暴力的受害者。奥马尔斯卡试图用三维动画中幸存者的档案材料、视频和陈述来构建一个虚拟的纪念馆。一旦最后一个证人死亡，文本和图像文件将在历史重新评估事件中起到中心作用。科学家、艺术家、电影制片人和作家将成为过去的翻译家，他们将不得不取代那些以自己的经验作为历史学家的幸存者。Bosnian War 1992. In the north of Bosnia and Herzegovina lies the concentration camp Omarska, which according to Serbian reports was an assembly point and investigation centre. Between May and August 1992, thousands of people were interned, tortured, raped and murdered there. Now it is a factory site of the Arcelor Mittal Company. So far, those murdered there have yet to be commemorated. The film is based on the agonizing memories of Nusreta Sivac, who served as a judge until the outbreak of the war. She was sent to the Omarska concentration camp and had to work in the kitchen. From there she could observe the atrocities and became a victim of the violence herself. Omarska tries to construct a virtual memorial using archive material, videos and statements by survivors in a 3D animation. As soon as the last witnesses have died, text and image documents will play a central role in the historical reappraisal of the events. Scientists, artists, filmmakers and writers will become interpreters of the past and will have to replace the survivors who were the historians of their own experience.
